In the probe, showerror on a StepError gives: init! for :boundary_zero, overlay! for :overlay, 'restore!(sim2, cp) of the same checkpoint reproduces it' for :restore, and 'replay! … then step!' for :loop. When the cause is an InterruptException, it prints 'an interrupt cut …, so nothing reproduces it; <door> runs it again / resumes from boundary 3' instead (src/diagnostics.jl:296-327). §13.4 states the init!, overlay! and halt-then-step! recipes (spec.md:11610-11658). No spec text and no docstring states the restore! recipe or the interrupt lines. The restore!, overlay! and init! docstrings only say an interrupt arrives as a StepError (src/sim.jl:815, 958, 1056). D-441, which the code comment cites, does not state the rendered recipe.
judgments.fix: Add to §13.4 after the overlay! sentence: "A throw inside the copy or the settling that `restore!` runs reproduces under `restore!` of the same checkpoint. An interrupt that cut a door or a frame reproduces nothing, so the rendered line names the door that runs the cut sequence again: `init!` or `overlay!` under the same condition, `restore!` of the same checkpoint, or for a frame `replay!` to the pointer, which resumes from the boundary the frame started at ([D-441][d-441])."

notes:
I checked all 28 claims read-only at W = 02745494: 15 conform and 13 do not. I edited no tracked file and committed nothing. I wrote one probe script and ran it once: /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/CV1_v/probe.jl. Every probe line cited in the judgments comes from that run.

How I ruled the map rows. code_map.md:8-12 says an entry names constructs, and adds 'For more, read the file itself'. On that ground the trial overturned C14-011. So I found that leaving out private helpers or constants does not break conformance: CV1-005, 008, 027, 090 and 124. CV1-105 is different, because that bullet lists 'the members of dataplane.jl's KINDS' and so claims to be complete.

How I ruled the Appendix C payload rows. Appendix C calls its payload column the acceptance-test contract (spec.md:15406-15409), and D-216 calls the column the design. Where the appendix names a payload item that no field holds and no sentence ties to another field, I found non-conformance: ClassMixed, GuardForm and EntryTypeMismatch. BindingContractMismatch conforms, because its entry says itself that the `reason` tells the cases apart.

Leads I found outside the claims:
(1) UninitializedInputs is listed in Appendix C as 'collected'. assert_total throws DiagnosticError(UninitializedInputs(...)), whose carrier type is the fail-fast DiagnosticError{UninitializedInputs} (src/conditions.jl:705). The collection lives inside the `faces` payload.
(2) BS3's constructor collects both tolerance refusals into DiagnosticError{Vector{Diagnostic}} (src/deployment.jl:416-423). Appendix C's ArgumentInvalid policy list does not name BS3 among the collected cases.
(3) The claim in CV1-124 misstates the code: conditions.jl never uses CHECKPOINT_ORIGIN. The claim in CV1-090 overstates it: src/sim.jl:1163 fills `legal` with a literal list.
